It opens a city written by 0.0.10 as it is (the Ledger's event-log version is still 2); 0.0.10 is not promised to read a Ledger that 0.0.11 has written, and the loopback port now asks every browser to pair, so a browser that worked with 0.0.10 pairs once more. ⚠️ **<!-- xtask:begin maturity:titled -->Alpha<!-- xtask:end -->。** sprawling <!-- xtask:begin workspace_version -->0.0.11<!-- xtask:end --> SIGNATURE 已经可用：它能从头到尾跑起一座城市，User 可以把真活交给它。它可以直接打开 0.0.10 写下的城市（账本格式版本仍是 2）；但 0.0.10 不保证能读 0.0.11 写过的账本，而且本地端口从这一版起也要求浏览器配对，0.0.10 用过的浏览器要再配对一次。替换已安装的二进制前，请先停止城市，并按[更新指南](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/blob/main/docs/getting-started.zh-CN.md#更新)验证更新前备份能恢复。

**What this version is for / 这一版做什么** — in the author's words, below in Chinese: from this version the Windows binary carries a code signature, thanks to SignPath; any agent that speaks ACP can join a city; the model · provider · thinking picker is redesigned; the terminal becomes a minimal CLI, and `/web` leaves only the address and a pairing code on screen; the loopback port no longer lets in a caller without a credential. Performance measurement is still open.

欢迎来到sprawling v0.0.11 Alpha 261009 (SIGNATURE)！
这个版本的头等大事当然是现在的sprawling agents从本版开始将拥有应用签名，感谢SignPath提供的签名！
第二重要的事情是sprawling agents从本版开始将支持接入任何支持ACP协议的Harness，具体的操作请见相关文档，但这也只是第一步。我听到有人说WebUI的极简风格很符合它的喜好，却因为（正如我们早就在之前的Release Note讨论过的）现在的模型都基于自家Harness进行RL（其实这样会导致模型过拟合问题），抗拒使用sprawling agents的内核（我一点也不伤心，骗你的）。不过反过来想想，sprawling agents的WebUI本身就允许任何用户自己设计，甚至担心源码对于目前一些LLM的智力不足还提供了充足的文档用于节省Token（当然也可以看一下Deepwiki对本项目生成的介绍），那为什么不能反过来让WebUI本身可以兼容任何的Harness呢？这里的问题在于，无论是先有前端还是先有后端，前后端一定要在一个统一的协议上面才能运作，wire层就负责链接client，但其他家的Harness没有任何理由兼容sprawling agents的wire层。但所幸我们有ACP协议充当了这个wire层。当然这件事**并没完全完成**，这个版本的核心是让任何支持ACP协议的Harness接入而非基于ACP让任何Agent使用WebUI，如果你们了解过T3Code（大概是为各种官方Harness提供一个统一UI调度层的代表项目），它实际上只支持了1，Codex CLI 2，Claude Code 3，Cursor CLI 4，Grok Build CLI 5，OpenCode 6，Antigravity 这六个。如果要把一个Harness真正意义上的做进WebUI，可能每一个都需要一个版本的工作量，因而这个版本只是小小的一步，代表项目整体会向着这个方向前进一步。与此同时，上一版相对不令人满意的Provider→Model/Thinking这个组件得到了重新设计，我将确保每个版本都对WebUI的某个不那么令我满意的组件进行修改（感谢上个版本咬牙完成了一个大工程，现在WebUI走向了组件式，也就是说其实你也可以只花几分钟修改某一个你不喜欢的组件然后继续用）
这个版本剩下的两件事大体上是一体的，现在项目有了个勉强能用的CLI，而启动WebUI从最快的启动终端+Enter变成了启动终端+/Web。上一版的CLI几乎是副作用，没人会用，我自己也不想盯着，反而还会把WebUI的工作记录呈现在上面成为一个额外的泄密面，同时如果工作到不小心关了浏览器还忘记了端口，重新打开又成了一件麻烦事。既然做到了隐私保密相关的内容，本版也顺手额外升级了一下隐私保护。之前的版本里，城市在127.0.0.1上开的端口几乎不设防，浏览器里随便哪个网页、哪段脚本都能连上来（localhost可不等于安全）。从这一版开始，每个来访者都得先出示凭据：`/web`打开的浏览器自动配对；换一个浏览器就输终端上的8位配对码，只给一次机会；`sprawling call`这类命令读你用户目录下只有你能读的密钥文件，脚本不用改。终端也剩地址和配对码两行，城市启动的子进程拿不到城市环境里的密钥，Agent的浏览器工具也打不开城市自己的页面了

当然，由于核心是上面的三件事，这一版依旧延后了性能测量和优化，不出意外的话我会尽快继续推进性能优化，并在下个月之前开始推进**生成式UI**前端的探索：归根结底目前所有Harness的UI都是为＜10Session设计，无论是会话列表，办公室，看板，Dashboard，分屏窗格，Agentic Inbox还是信箱……我们必须承认在真正的规模化工作中，它们都落后于时代了。我不会说类似于“dashboard is dead”这种话毕竟还有很多场景它们是通用解法，大家的习惯也建立于上面，但对于我们讨论的这个规模化Agent场景或claude code推出dynamic workflow之后的超大规模全自动化agentic工作场景，它们的确都已经该死了。而且人们忽视了这里的学习成本，的确它们常用，但学习一个新的管理方式，或者一个定制化的管理方式，成本绝对和面对一次布局改版和添加几个必要的插件相同，这还是建立在维护者深入研究了UI/UX的基础上。严格来说我们并不知道到底什么样的UI才是最适合Muti-Agent环境，或者说这个环境并没有最适合的一种方案而只有对具体的某个用户+项目最清晰的方案。所以生成式UI并非为了炫技或者更加个性化而是严格来说我们并没有一个足够好的交互方案能真正动态地实现注意力管理和信息整理，我们的UI是静态的代码，而Muti-Agent环境需要面对的是动态的规划、实践和反馈的循环。当然实践起来大概会分成几个阶段，先从对话中生成交互小组件开始，再逐步变成一个完整的方案，这里有太多细节和方案有待探索了，说不定最后会变成科幻电影里的仪表盘（根据我对于LLM的理解，概率不低）。除此之外，可能还会补一些内容，目前接入ASR模型后会有一个麦克风的内容，但严格来说口喷Prompt一直是一个我很反感的内容，我认为这里是一个巨大的错误（在AI自动化写作之前，我经常拉黑的博主就主要是用语音转文字发专栏的，想象一下LLM的工作原理和小ASR模型的识别正确率，我认为这和工作时给LLM一个毫无意义的人设一样抽象）。我们需要的是那种有点智力（例如0.5T水平？）真正及时回复然后派单的模型而不是ASR+LLM，ASR模型真正的用处是剪辑/computer use等场景。另外一边同步两条线，一个是老生常谈的**Context Engineering**：会逐步探索目前可行的几个渐进式披露方案，用于管理MCP/ACP/A2A/SKILL等膨大的System Prompt问题，这个会成为性能之外对于规模化非常重要的优化。另外一边sprawling v0.0.10 Alpha 261008 (INNOCENT)的Release Note讨论了**Personal Agent**的各种问题，的确似乎要便利的Personal Agent就似乎必须把个人隐私交给大公司去管理，用广告当一部分补贴。但我相信肯定肯定也有人愿意花时间配置，花钱运营一个个性化的Personal Agent（这里可能有一点学习成本，实际跑起来说不定运营成本考虑到订阅和工作必要开支和大公司的方案差不了多少甚至有得省）。那么在未来的某个版本，V0.1.0之前我会正式研究沙箱问题，一方面是处理Agent本身的权限与安全问题，另一方面则是基于沙箱运行手机/平板模拟器使用内置无障碍+截图/录制+仿真点击补上**Phone use**的缺口。其他的就在Changing Log或Commit记录里面看吧，上一版就留下了那么多ToDo，世界变化如此之快，又有着如此之多的限制，谁又知道下一版又是什么内容呢？ <!-- lexicon-ok: the author's own word in his release note, quoted and not changed -->
さて、どこへ行こうかしらね。ネットは広大だわ。

---

**In English / 英文版**

Welcome to sprawling v0.0.11 Alpha 261009 (SIGNATURE)!
The most important thing in this version is of course that, from this version on, sprawling agents has an application signature; thanks to SignPath for the signing!
The second most important thing is that, from this version on, sprawling agents supports connecting any harness that supports the ACP protocol; see the related documentation for the steps, but this too is only the first step. I heard someone say that the minimal style of the WebUI suits their taste, but that because (as we discussed long ago in an earlier release note) today's models are all trained with RL on their own vendor's harness (which in fact makes the models overfit), they resist using the sprawling agents core (I am not sad at all; just kidding). But think about it the other way round: the sprawling agents WebUI already lets any user design it themselves, and, in case the source is beyond the intelligence of some current LLMs, it even provides ample documentation to save tokens (you can also look at the introduction DeepWiki generated for this project), so why can the WebUI itself not be made compatible with any harness? The problem is that whether the front end or the back end comes first, the two can only work on one shared protocol; the wire layer links the client, but other vendors' harnesses have no reason at all to be compatible with sprawling agents' wire layer. Fortunately we have the ACP protocol to act as this wire layer. Of course this is **not fully done**: the core of this version is letting any harness that supports ACP connect, not letting any Agent use the WebUI through ACP. If you know T3Code (roughly the representative project that gives the various official harnesses one unified UI scheduling layer), it actually supports only these six: 1. Codex CLI, 2. Claude Code, 3. Cursor CLI, 4. Grok Build CLI, 5. OpenCode, 6. Antigravity. Building a harness into the WebUI in the real sense may take one version's work for each, so this version is only a small step, which means the project as a whole moves one step in that direction. At the same time, the Provider→Model/Thinking component, which was rather unsatisfying in the last version, has been redesigned. I will make sure every version changes some WebUI component I am not so happy with (thanks to the big job the last version gritted its teeth to finish, the WebUI is now component-based, which means you too can spend just a few minutes changing a component you dislike and keep using it).
The remaining two things in this version are largely one: the project now has a CLI that is barely usable, and starting the WebUI has gone from the fastest "start a terminal + Enter" to "start a terminal + /Web". The last version's CLI was almost a side effect: nobody would use it, I did not want to stare at it myself, and it even showed the WebUI's work records, which made it an extra leak surface; and if, while working, you closed the browser by accident and had forgotten the port, opening it again became a chore. Since we were working on privacy and secrecy anyway, this version also gave privacy protection an extra upgrade along the way. In earlier versions the port the city opened on 127.0.0.1 was almost unguarded: any web page or script in your browser could connect to it (localhost does not mean safe). From this version on, every caller has to present a credential first: the browser `/web` opens pairs on its own; another browser types the 8-character pairing code the terminal shows, and gets one chance; commands such as `sprawling call` read a key file in your user directory that only you can read, so scripts need no change. For browsers I did not use cookies, because cookies are not separated by port; the page generates a device key of its own that cannot be exported. The terminal also shows only two lines, the address and the pairing code; the child processes the city starts do not get the keys in the city's environment; and an Agent's browser tool can no longer open the city's own pages. Of course all this guards against web pages and other callers, not against programs running under your own account, and an ACP Agent you add is such a program, so read the command line on the consent card before adding one (the same reasoning as not putting a camera in the bedroom); and these credentials only decide who gets through the door, they do not encrypt the local connection.

A few small things: the default thinking level is now high; if the model does not offer high, the provider's stated default is used, and if the upstream says nothing the field is not written; turning thinking off is no longer a level. The WebUI's default shortcuts that collided with the browser's own (Ctrl+P to print, Ctrl+1 to 6 to switch tabs, and so on) are gone, the command palette moved to Ctrl+/ (⌘+/ on a Mac), and you can bind whatever you want in Settings; the CLI binds no Ctrl chord, and the only way to close the city is `/quit`; features new in this version have no shortcuts either, and the next version completes them. Finally, the City is now written 城市 instead of 城 in the Chinese interface.

Of course, since the core is the three things above, this version again postpones performance measurement and optimisation. If nothing goes wrong I will continue the performance work as soon as I can, and before next month begin exploring a **generative UI** front end: in the end, every harness's UI today is designed for fewer than 10 sessions, whether it is a session list, an office, a kanban board, a dashboard, a grid of split panes, an agentic inbox or a mailbox… We have to admit that in truly large-scale work they have all fallen behind the times. I will not say something like "dashboard is dead", since there are still many scenarios where they are the general solution and everyone's habits are built on them, but for the large-scale agent work we are discussing, or the very large, fully automated agentic work that came after Claude Code launched dynamic workflows, they really do all deserve to die. And people overlook the learning cost here: yes, they are common, but learning a new way of managing, or a customised one, costs absolutely the same as facing one layout redesign and adding a few necessary plugins, and that is assuming the maintainer has studied UI/UX in depth. Strictly speaking we do not know what kind of UI best suits a multi-agent environment, or rather this environment has no single best solution, only the clearest solution for a particular user and project. So generative UI is not for showing off or for more personalisation; strictly speaking, we do not have an interaction design good enough to truly manage attention and organise information dynamically. Our UI is static code, while a multi-agent environment faces a dynamic loop of planning, practice and feedback. In practice it will probably come in stages: first generating small interactive widgets from the conversation, then gradually growing into a complete solution. There are far too many details and options still to explore here; it might even end up as the dashboard in a science-fiction film (from my understanding of LLMs, the odds are not low). Besides this, some more things may be added. Once an ASR model is connected there will be a microphone feature, but strictly speaking spoken prompts have always been something I strongly dislike, and I think they are a huge mistake (before AI automated writing, the bloggers I blocked most often were mainly the ones who published columns through speech-to-text; think about how LLMs work and how accurately small ASR models recognise speech: I think it is as absurd as giving an LLM a meaningless persona at work). What we need is a model with some intelligence (say at the 0.5T level?) that really replies in time and then dispatches the work, not ASR+LLM; the real use of ASR models is in scenarios such as video editing and computer use. Meanwhile two lines run in parallel. One is the familiar **Context Engineering**: I will gradually explore the few progressive-disclosure schemes that are workable today, to manage the bloated system prompts of MCP/ACP/A2A/SKILL; besides performance, this will become a very important optimisation for scale. On the other side, the release note of sprawling v0.0.10 Alpha 261008 (INNOCENT) discussed the various problems of the **Personal Agent**: it does seem that to have a convenient Personal Agent you must hand your personal privacy to a big company to manage, with ads paying for part of it. But I believe there are surely people willing to spend time configuring and money running a personalised Personal Agent (there may be some learning cost here; once it actually runs, the running cost, counting subscriptions and the expenses work requires anyway, may not differ much from the big companies' offers, and might even save money). So in some future version, before v0.1.0, I will formally study the sandbox problem: on one side to handle the Agent's own permissions and security, and on the other to run phone and tablet emulators in the sandbox and use built-in accessibility plus screenshots/recording plus simulated taps to fill the **Phone use** gap. For everything else, look at the Changelog or the commit history. The last version already left so many ToDos; the world changes so fast and has so many limits, who knows what the next version will bring?
さて、どこへ行こうかしらね。ネットは広大だわ。 ("Now, where shall I go? The net is vast.")

---

**Notes / 补充**

- **The loopback port / 本地端口** — Every caller of the city's port presents a credential, on `127.0.0.1` as from outside. The browser `/web` opens pairs without typing; another browser types the pairing code the terminal shows; a browser that worked with 0.0.10 pairs once more. A browser that cannot make an Ed25519 device key cannot pair and is told which browsers can. Settings list the paired browsers, and forgetting one closes its open pages at once. `sprawling call`, `dispatch`, `gauge` and `enrol` read the key file the city writes in the per-user runtime directory, but only when `--at` names this machine, so scripts that use them need no change; a script or tool that opened `ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/ws` without a credential is now refused and must read that file.

  城市的端口对每个来访者都要凭据，`127.0.0.1` 也一样。`/web` 打开的浏览器免输入配对；别的浏览器输入终端显示的配对码；0.0.10 用过的浏览器要再配对一次。做不出 Ed25519 设备密钥的浏览器无法配对，页面会说明换哪种浏览器。设置里列出已配对的浏览器，忘记其中一个会立刻关闭它打开的页面。`sprawling call`、`dispatch`、`gauge`、`enrol` 读城市写在每用户运行目录里的密钥文件，但只在 `--at` 指向这台电脑时才读，所以用到它们的脚本不用改；不带凭据直接连 `ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/ws` 的脚本或工具会被拒绝，要改为读这个文件。

- **The CLI and `/quit` / CLI 与 `/quit`** — `sprawling` with no arguments opens the CLI, and `/web` there opens the page. `sprawling up <dir>` and the release archive's launcher open the page and leave the terminal as the quiet host, which shows the address and the pairing code; Enter there opens the page again and Esc turns the terminal into the CLI. `/quit`, in the CLI or on a page this computer opened, is the only way to close the city, and closing the browser closes nothing.

  不带参数的 `sprawling` 打开 CLI，在里面用 `/web` 打开页面。`sprawling up <dir>` 和发行包里的启动器会打开页面，终端变为安静宿主，只显示地址和配对码；在那里按 Enter 重新打开页面，按 Esc 进入 CLI。关闭城市只能用 `/quit`，在 CLI 里或在这台电脑打开的页面里都可以；关掉浏览器不会关闭任何东西。

- **Thinking level / 思考强度** — The default is high where the model offers it, else the provider's stated default, else no level is sent. The level the picker stores is the city's own setting, kept apart from the model, and a model that lacks it falls back to that rule instead of refusing the message. `minimal` is new and `none` is no longer offered; a Ledger that recorded `none` still reads back. A level named with `/effort <level>` that the model does not offer is refused before dispatch. An endpoint attached under 0.0.10 offers only the vendor-documentation levels, or none, until it is attached again or its models are refreshed.

  默认是 high（模型提供时），否则用供应商声明的默认档，再否则不发档位。选择器存下的档位是城市自己的设置，和模型分开存；换到不提供这一档的模型时按上面的规则回退，不会拒绝消息。新增 `minimal`，不再提供 `none`；记过 `none` 的账本照样读回。用 `/effort <level>` 明确指定、而当前模型不提供的档位，在派活前被拒绝。0.0.10 时登记的端点，在重新登记或刷新模型之前，只提供厂商文档里的档位，或者不提供。

- **ACP agents / ACP agent** — Any agent that speaks ACP can be added from the ACP page or `/acp`: an agent found on this computer, an entry of the registry catalog shipped with the release, or a pasted command line, Zed or JetBrains `agent_servers` block, or registry `agent.json`. Nothing runs before you consent on its card, which shows the exact command line. The city does not start an agent's login in this release, and it never starts a claude.ai subscription login: an agent that needs a login is refused with the agent's own sign-in methods, so sign in with the agent's own program and send the task again. Registry agents distributed as binary archives are not downloaded or installed; install one yourself and it is detected, or paste its command.

  任何说 ACP 的 agent 都可以从 ACP 页或 `/acp` 添加：这台电脑上找到的、随版本附带的 registry 目录里的，或者粘贴一行命令、一段 Zed 或 JetBrains 的 `agent_servers`、一份 registry 的 `agent.json`。确认卡上写着确切的命令行，你确认之前什么都不会运行。本版城市不代为启动 agent 的登录，也从不代为启动 claude.ai 订阅登录：需要登录的 agent 会被拒绝，并列出它自己的登录方式，用 agent 自己的程序登录后再发一次任务即可。以二进制压缩包发行的 registry agent 不会被下载或安装；自己装好后会被检测到，或者直接粘贴它的命令。

- **Terminal status (OSC 7501) / 终端状态（OSC 7501）** — The Program Status Protocol is a terminal escape sequence Mitchell Hashimoto published on 2026-10-06, with revision 0.3 the next day: a program tells the terminal it runs in whether it is idle, working, blocked on the user, done or failed, and why, and the terminal decides how to show it. It exists because the tools that watch many agents at once, such as Herdr or cmux, guess an agent's state by matching its screen or window title, and those rules break whenever an agent changes its spinner; a socket API for each tool does not cross SSH or a container, and the pty already does. libghostty, Rex, Bubble Tea 2.1.0, Claude Code 2.1.295 and Pi 1.1.0 implement it. In the CLI and the quiet host, sprawling now reports one record for the whole city: `blocked` while a request waits for an answer, `working` while a run is going, and otherwise `done`, `error` or `idle` after how the last run ended; the message carries counts such as "2 runs are going" and never a word from the history, and the record is cleared when the city closes. An ACP agent the city seats runs over a pipe with no terminal, so it sends no OSC 7501 there; its turns are the city's runs and count in the city's record. The city sends no support query first, because the CLI's input reader would type the terminal's answer into the prompt; the protocol allows that, a terminal that does not know the sequence ignores it, and `SPRAWLING_PROGRAM_STATUS=never` turns it off. Adoption is early: tmux's maintainer called it premature until more terminals and programs take it up, and Cargo's maintainers are waiting for the same; Rex, the protocol author's own terminal, plans to push records to its phone app and gather them in one view ordered by priority. Once terminals group child records, one record per room is the next step for the city.

  Program Status Protocol 是 Mitchell Hashimoto 在 2026-10-06 发布的一条终端转义序列，第二天出了 rev 0.3：程序告诉它所在的终端，自己是空闲、在跑、等人处理、已完成还是失败了，以及原因，怎么显示由终端决定。需要它，是因为同时盯着很多 agent 的工具（比如 Herdr、cmux）靠匹配屏幕内容或窗口标题去猜 agent 的状态，agent 换一个转圈字符，规则就失效；给每个工具各开一个 socket API，又过不了 SSH 和容器，而 pty 本来就能过。libghostty、Rex、Bubble Tea 2.1.0、Claude Code 2.1.295 和 Pi 1.1.0 已经实现了它。sprawling 现在在 CLI 和安静宿主里为整座城市报告一条记录：有请求等人回答时是 `blocked`，有 run 在跑时是 `working`，否则按最后一个结束的 run 报 `done`、`error` 或 `idle`；消息里只有「2 runs are going」这样的计数，不带历史里的任何字，城市关闭时记录被清掉。城市经 ACP 接入的 agent 走管道、没有终端，在城市里不会发 OSC 7501；它们的每一轮就是城市的一个 run，计在城市的那条记录里。城市不先发支持查询，因为 CLI 的输入解析器会把终端的回答当成键入的字；协议允许这样做，不认识这条序列的终端会忽略它，`SPRAWLING_PROGRAM_STATUS=never` 可以关掉。这条协议还很新：tmux 的维护者认为现在支持为时过早，要先看还有没有别的终端和程序跟进，Cargo 的维护者也在等生态的反应；协议作者自己的终端 Rex 打算把这些记录推到手机 app，并汇总到一个按轻重排序的视图里。等终端开始按子记录分组显示，城市的下一步是每个房间一条记录。

- **Shortcuts / 快捷键** — Every WebUI default that took a browser's own key in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari lost its default; the palette moved to Ctrl+/ (⌘+/), and any action can be bound in Settings. Features new in this release have no shortcut; the next version completes them.

  WebUI 默认快捷键里，凡是占了 Chrome、Edge、Firefox 或 Safari 自带按键的，都去掉了默认绑定；命令面板移到 Ctrl+/（⌘+/），任何动作都可以在设置里自己绑定。本版新增的功能没有快捷键，下一版补齐。

- **城市** — The Chinese interface, the Chinese README and the Chinese getting-started guide call the City 城市 instead of 城.

  中文界面、中文 README 和中文入门指南把「城」改成了「城市」。

- **Building from crates.io on Windows / Windows 上从 crates.io 构建** — `cargo install sprawling` on Windows needs Zig 0.17.0 on PATH; the prebuilt channels do not.

  Windows 上 `cargo install sprawling` 需要 PATH 里有 Zig 0.17.0；预构建渠道不需要。

- **Backward compatibility / 向后兼容** — The Ledger's event-log version is still 2; the wire moved from WIRE_V 64 to 65, and an old browser tab is refused rather than misread. A snapshot cut by an earlier build of the views is refused by version and rebuilt from the Ledger.

  账本格式版本仍是 2；协议从 WIRE_V 64 升到 65，旧标签页会被明确拒绝而不是读错。旧版本切下的视图快照按版本被拒绝，再从账本重建。

- **Known limits / 已知限制** — A process running as your account, which includes an ACP agent you added, can read the key file and drive the city. A crash can leave child processes running. "Stop now" ends a run within a time limit but does not cancel a model call already in flight. An upstream that refuses a level it stated is not remembered.

  以你的账户运行的进程，包括你添加的 ACP agent，能读到密钥文件并操作城市。崩溃后子进程可能还在运行。「立刻停下」会在限定时间内结束 run，但不会取消已经发出的模型调用。上游拒绝了它自己声明过的档位，这件事不会被记住。

**What comes next** (not necessarily all in the next version; finishing them does not by itself make v0.1.0 Beta, and no version or date is promised):

- Checks and small improvements: 1. performance measurement and optimisation; 2. WebUI shortcuts, completed in the next version; 3. signing in to an ACP agent from the city, and installing registry agents distributed as binary archives; 4. one more WebUI component redesigned in each version.
- Features: 1. generative UI; 2. Context Engineering, progressive disclosure for MCP/ACP/A2A/SKILL; 3. before v0.1.0, a sandbox for the Agent's own permissions and for Phone use.

---

**Maturity ladder / 成熟度阶梯**

| Stage | Version | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| pre-alpha | 0.0.x | runs end to end; nothing is promised |
| alpha | 0.0.x | usable / 可用 |
| beta | 0.1.0 | good to use / 好用 |
| stable | 1.0.0 | no compromise on experience or on long-term maintenance, with a mature maintainer or team / 体验与长期维护都不妥协，维护者或团队成熟 |
